handoff.purpose: Task preparation entry point: infer paths, route to agent, record memory, optionally enqueue Claude request, and expose a CLI.

symbols.name: _infer_paths
symbols.note: Infers filesystem paths from a text string by tokenizing on spaces, commas, and backticks, stripping quotes/brackets/parens, resolving relative paths against the repo root, and keeping only existing paths (deduplicated preserving order).

symbols.name: prepare_task
symbols.note: Resolves repo root, loads project data, trims/infers paths, routes to an agent, collects git status, appends a MemoryEvent (user_task, status open), optionally enqueues a Claude request, and returns a dict with all relevant results.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entry point: parses arguments and calls prepare_task, printing the result as pretty-printed JSON.

observations.what: _infer_paths treats any token containing a dot in its filename as a path, even if it is not a real filesystem path (e.g., 'foo.bar' becomes a candidate). But it only appends existing candidates, so the impact is limited to unnecessary filesystem checks.
_infer_paths deduplicates paths using dict.fromkeys, which preserves order in Python 3.7+.
prepare_task calls collect_status(root) but the status is only used in the return dict and the memory payload; it is not used for any decision in this chunk.
The memory payload includes 'agent' and 'git_status' but does not include the project data or the strategy, which might be relevant for auditing.
The enqueue call uses project_data.get('claude_model', 'sonnet') but if project_data is empty (no project specified), it defaults to 'sonnet'.
The CLI has no --no-enqueue option; ask_claude is only controlled by --no-claude, which is a boolean flag. There is no way to disable the memory event or the status collection.

The CLI prints the result dict as JSON. The dict includes Path objects (repo_root, queued_claude_request) which are not JSON-serializable by default; json.dumps will raise TypeError unless a custom serializer is provided. This is a likely runtime error for the CLI.
The 'queued_claude_request' value is a string (from str(enqueue(...))), but 'repo_root' is a Path object (from resolve_repo_root). json.dumps will fail on Path.

The 'paths' list may contain Path objects? No, _infer_paths returns strings, trim_paths is called on them; the result is a list of strings. But the 'repo_root' is a Path object, and 'memory_event' might be a MemoryEvent object (not JSON-serializable). The CLI will likely fail on serialization.
